title: Generic factorizations, models and centred valuation points
statement: Let $T$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $L$ a field [def-weil-field], and $\eta:\operatorname{Spec}L\to T$ a morphism [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. A generic factorization of $\eta$ consists of an integral scheme $X$ [def-pc-integral-scheme], morphisms $p:X\to T$ and $g:\operatorname{Spec}L\to X$, such that the unique point of $\operatorname{Spec}L$ maps to the generic point of $X$ and $p\circ g=\eta$. A model is a generic factorization with $p$ proper [def-weil-proper-morphism]. A quasi-model is a generic factorization with $p$ separated and of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], with separatedness as in [def-weil-proper-morphism]. A morphism from a model $M$ to a model $N$ is a morphism $h:X_M\to X_N$ satisfying $p_N\circ h=p_M$ and $h\circ g_M=g_N$. A valuation point over $(T,L,\eta)$ consists of a valuation subring $V\subseteq L$ (a subring containing $a$ or $a^{-1}$ for every nonzero $a\in L$) and a morphism $c:\operatorname{Spec}V\to T$ whose composition with the spectrum map of $V\hookrightarrow L$ is $\eta$. For a quasi-model $U$, composition with $p_U$ defines the push map from valuation points over $(X_U,L,g_U)$ to valuation points over $(T,L,\eta)$: it retains $V$ and replaces $c$ by $p_U\circ c$. These are structures and an explicit composition map for arbitrary $T,L,\eta$; no existence, compactness or finite-refinement assertion is included.
